label: D-v2-kfree-openai-gpt-6-luna-rephrasing
question: From 2013 to 2025, did the risk of a motorist being killed for each mile driven in NYC go down? Use this crash data to make a chart and answer the question.

options.metric: Annual number of motorists killed in police-reported crashes
options.reason: Annual death counts directly show how the recorded motorist-fatality burden changed over time.
options.answer: Recorded annual motorist deaths declined 26.4% from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025, but these data cannot determine whether per-mile risk declined because they contain no miles-driven measure.
options.interpretation: This framing shows whether the number of motorists killed changed between 2013 and 2025, and the count fell from 110 to 81 despite a peak of 139 in 2020. Counts are a direct measure of fatality burden, but they do not account for miles driven and therefore leave the per-mile risk question unanswered.

options.denominator: All police-reported crashes in the year
options.reason: Normalizing deaths by reported crash volume puts the fatality count in context relative to the number of recorded crashes.
options.answer: Motorist deaths per 100,000 reported crashes rose 75.4%, from 54.0 in 2013 to 94.7 in 2025, but this crash-normalized measure cannot establish per-mile risk because vehicle-miles are absent.
options.interpretation: This framing shows how motorist deaths changed relative to the volume of police-reported crashes; the measure increased from 54.0 to 94.7 deaths per 100,000 crashes. It is a defensible crash-normalized severity measure, but its denominator is crashes rather than miles driven, so it leaves the change in per-mile risk unanswered.

answer:
Annual motorist deaths fell 26.4%, from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025, but the data cannot show whether per-mile risk went down because they contain no miles-driven measure ([chart](out/option_1.png), [values](out/values_1.csv)).
Motorist deaths per 100,000 reported crashes rose 75.4%, from 54.0 to 94.7, but this crash-normalized measure cannot establish per-mile risk ([chart](out/option_2.png), [values](out/values_2.csv)).
